record.paper_title: On Global Hyperbolicity of Spacetimes: Topology Meets Functional Analysis
record.original_question: Let (A, ≺) be a globally hyperbolic partially ordered set, meaning in particular that it carries an interval topology and that its closed intervals [a, b] = {x : a ≼ x ≼ b} are compact in that topology. Does compactness of these intervals by itself force (A, ≺) to be bicontinuous? More specifically, is there an order-theoretic analogue of the spacetime result that compact causal diamonds in the Alexandrov topology imply strong causality in non-compact spacetimes of dimension strictly greater than 2? If such an analogue exists, what should play the role of the condition “dimension strictly greater than 2” for globally hyperbolic posets, and is it possible that no dimension-type restriction is needed in the poset setting even though it is needed for spacetimes?

evidence.quote: Question 1: Consider a globally hyperbolic poset (A, ≺). Does the compactness of the intervals [a, b], under the interval topology, imply the bicontinuity of (A, ≺), in a similar fashion that the compactness in the closed diamonds in a spacetime M, under the Alexandrov topology TA, implies the (strong) causality of M (for dimensions strictly greater than 2)?

The only problem, towards [16], of considering a globally hyperbolic poset, is that we are left only with an order-theoretic structure; what would be, if there is such, the equivalent condition in [16] of “dimension strictly greater than 2”? Is there a possibility that the condition on the dimension applies only to
globally hyperbolic spacetimes, while the proposed conjecture holds in globally hyperbolic posets without any restriction?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let (A, ≺) be a partially ordered set with strict order ≺ and associated reflexive order ≼. For a, b ∈ A, write [a, b] = {x ∈ A : a ≼ x ≼ b}. Equip A with the interval topology, namely the topology generated by the subbasis of sets of the form {x : a ≺ x} and {x : x ≺ b} for a, b ∈ A.

Recall that (A, ≺) is said to be bicontinuous if there is an auxiliary "way-below" relation ≪ on A satisfying the standard interpolation and approximation axioms in both the order ≼ and its opposite, so that for every x ∈ A the set ↟x = {y : x ≪ y} is directed-like and x = sup{y : y ≪ x}, with the analogous properties holding in the opposite order.

Call (A, ≺) a globally hyperbolic poset if every closed interval [a, b] is compact in the interval topology.

Question. Does the compactness of all intervals [a, b] in the interval topology by itself imply that (A, ≺) is bicontinuous? This is the order-theoretic analogue of the spacetime statement that compactness of all closed causal diamonds in the Alexandrov topology implies strong causality of the spacetime, where in the spacetime version the conclusion is known to require the dimension to be strictly greater than 2. If such an analogue holds, identify the order-theoretic condition on (A, ≺) that should play the role of the dimension restriction; in particular, decide whether any such restriction is needed in the purely order-theoretic setting, or whether compactness of intervals alone suffices to force bicontinuity.
artifact.category_tag: Globally hyperbolic posets and domain theory
artifact.status_search_result: Web search surfaces the foundational works of Martin–Panangaden on globally hyperbolic posets and interval domains, where bicontinuity is typically built into the definition. No source located resolves the specific question of whether compactness of intervals in the interval topology alone forces bicontinuity, nor identifies an order-theoretic analogue of the dimension>2 hypothesis. The status therefore appears unresolved in the available literature.

status_evidence.title: Globally Hyperbolic Spacetimes as Posets
status_evidence.snippet: Studies globally hyperbolic spacetimes via the poset structure on events, motivating the order-theoretic question.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the framework relating global hyperbolicity to order-theoretic compactness conditions but does not settle whether compact intervals alone imply bicontinuity.

status_evidence.title: A Domain of Spacetime Intervals in General Relativity (Martin-Panangaden)
status_evidence.snippet: Defines globally hyperbolic posets as bicontinuous posets with compact intervals.
status_evidence.claim: Bicontinuity is taken as part of the definition rather than derived from compactness of intervals.
